items.question: What is synthetic doe in estrus scent?
items.answer: Synthetic doe estrus scent is a hunting attractant that replicates the pheromone signature a whitetail doe releases during her estrus (breeding) cycle. It signals to mature bucks that a receptive doe is nearby, drawing them to your hunting location. Odin's uses 100% synthetic formulations—no natural deer urine—ensuring consistent potency and zero risk of CWD transmission.

items.question: When should I start using doe in estrus scent?
items.answer: Begin using doe estrus when bucks in your area enter the seeking phase—typically late October in Northern states and sometimes twice in SE States. Using it too early, before local does are actually entering estrus, may spook mature bucks. Peak effectiveness is during the main rut in November. In Southern states, adjust timing to match local breeding dates, which may be as late as January or February. Use Odin's Scrape Blend prior to the actual rut.

items.question: Is deer urine legal to use in my state for hunting?
items.answer: Maybe. There is no single, centralized consumer-facing resource that definitively covers the legality of natural cervid urine across all U.S. states. The regulatory landscape is a fragmented, state-by-state patchwork with no federal oversight body governing cervid urine production or use.

items.question: How to use doe estrus scent beads instead of liquid?
items.answer: Odin's scent beads are designed to be dispersed on the ground in the area to which you want to attract your deer. Spread out the beads in a 4' X 4' area and they will release the scent for 30-days. When using a typical liquid scent, you pour it on the ground. Then, next time you go out you replace the liquid again.

items.question: Where are the Odin's products made?
items.answer: Everything is made in the United States! The scents, the polymer beads, the blending and packaging, too.

items.question: When is the doe estrus scent most effective?
items.answer: Peak rut refers to the period when the highest percentage of does in a given area are entering estrus simultaneously. This population-level peak typically spans 10–14 days and is driven by photoperiod—declining daylight triggers hormonal cascades across the doe population. It's not a single-day event, which is why sustained scent presence through Odin's 30-day beads outperforms single-application and quickly depreciating products.

items.question: Where should I place doe estrus scent?
items.answer: In scrapes, mock scrapes, or hang in mesh bags along travel corridors, bedding edges, and near stand sites.

items.question: Is synthetic doe estrus as effective as real doe urine?
items.answer: Yes. Our synthetic formulations are engineered to precise molecular specifications by a specialty fragrance laboratory and have been field-tested over 10 hunting seasons. Unlike natural urine, which varies in concentration from sample to sample and degrades after bottling, synthetic estrous delivers identical pheromone concentration every time.

items.question: How do you know the natural deer urine was collected during the estrus cycle?
items.answer: We don't know....the results from your hunt would certainly imply the answer. An individual doe's estrus—the period during which she is receptive to breeding—typically lasts approximately 24–48 hours, with many sources narrowing it to around 24–30 hours. If she is not bred during that cycle, she will recycle roughly 28 days later. A figure of 36 hours is a reasonable midpoint estimate for a single doe's receptive window.

items.question: Why not use natural urine scents?
items.answer: Natural urine breaks down rapidly into ammonia and other off odors that can actually alarm him. Natural scents vary from batch to batch, requires refrigeration, and has a short effective life. Synthetic scents avoid spoilage, maintain a consistent aroma profile, last 30+ days, and carry zero CWD risk.

items.question: How do I know a synthetic scent is actually accurate?
items.answer: Field performance is the only proof that matters — and Odin's has more of it than anyone. Our synthetic formulations were first introduced in 2018, making them the longest field-proven synthetic scents on the market. Deer knows when something's not quite right, and seven-plus seasons of documented results confirm our scents pass that test. The growth in synthetic adoption isn't driven by regulation alone — it's driven by hunters finding products that actually work. Look for field-tested performance history, not just a 'synthetic' label.

items.question: Can I use dominant buck scent and doe estrus together?
items.answer: Absolutely. Using both together creates the most compelling scenario for a mature buck: the scent of a rival male with a receptive doe. Odin's Scrape Blend combines both in a single product for exactly this purpose. You can also deploy them separately—dominant buck on one side of your setup, doe estrus on the other—to create directional scent fields.

items.question: How do I set up a trail back to my tree stand?
items.answer: Hunters have shared a lot of creative approaches: (1) squirt the liquid on the bottom of your boots as you walk in, (2) squirt it on your eBike tires, (3) squirt the liquid on foliage as you traverse, letting the wind carry the scent, and (4) sprinkle a small amount of beads 5–10 feet apart on the path.

items.question: How long does Odin's doe estrus scent last?
items.answer: Odin's scent beads release scent continuously for 30+ days. University laboratory testing confirmed that after 27 days, our biodegradable polymer was still releasing 52% of its original scent concentration. The beads are also impervious to moisture—rain, snow, and heavy dew will not wash the scent away. The liquid formula lasts 7–10 days per application.

items.question: Are Odin's scent beads biodegradable?
items.answer: Yes. Odin's scent beads are the only scent or attractant available that is made from a plant-based biodegradable polymer that breaks down completely when left on the ground. Exactly how long it takes to fully biodegrade depends on the elements.....a good point of reference is how long it might take for a banana peel to degrade.
